raw_text: {"anchor":"my cousin","spark":"spring hike","wound":"annoyance","fuel":"someone you like","bridge":"plan is a suggestion","echo":"closure sign","narrative":"there is a short hike i did one spring with my cousin that i keep forgetting and then remembering. the trail was closed past the second bridge, so what was meant to be a loop became an out-and-back of about an hour, and we spent half of it debating whether the closure sign applied to people who were already on the far side of it. i was the one carrying the map nobody looked at, and my calves burned on the last switchback going back up; i remember being annoyed about that in a way the hill did not deserve. if i take anything from that afternoon, it is that a plan is a suggestion the weather has not read yet, and that a short walk with someone you like is still a short walk with someone you like, even when the loop does not close."}

raw_text: {"anchor":"dawn bird walk","spark":"missing the heron","wound":"missed moment","fuel":"kingfisher","bridge":"go again next month","echo":"same group, different lot","narrative":"went on the dawn bird walk this morning and thought it was mixed results. they saw a lot of the usual suspects and a kingfisher, which was great, but the rest of the group watched a heron take off about two minutes before they got there because they parked at the wrong lot and had to walk round. they said that one was on them because they read the map upside down, and the guide being very nice about it somehow made it worse. the rest of the walk was quiet, with the guide knowing every call before the bird was visible, and they spent the second half trying to tell two very similar warblers apart. they said they might go again next month, then made coffee and moved on to a very ordinary weekend."}
